## Purpose

An `Observer` in `apps/rt/src/hooks` is a unit struct (`ApprovalMarkerObserver`, `PickerApprovalObserver`, `PlanApprovalObserver`) whose `observe()` method returns `()` and never a verdict — per the crate Guard, observers are pure side-effect/telemetry and blocking decisions live exclusively in a `Check`. Each of the three approval-marker observers mints the SAME `<spec>/.approved-by-user` marker through a shared `marker_body`/`approval_marker_path` helper, but through a DIFFERENT unforgeable trigger (`AskUserQuestion`, `ExitPlanMode`, a picker slash-command prompt), and each is fail-closed on any doubt about whether the signal is genuinely user-authored, while being fail-open on IO (a write that cannot happen is silently skipped, never panics or blocks the session). The module doc is where the security reasoning is spelled out at length — which facts must ALL hold before anything is recorded, and which forged/edge cases were closed in the field.

## Convention

Folder: apps/rt/src/hooks/** · Extension: .rs · Files of this role in this subproject: 18

Beyond the census facts: the file opens with an extensive `//!` doc laying out numbered "facts" that must ALL hold before the observer records anything, generally including a "why this is unforgeable" argument and a description of the forged/incident case the observer was hardened against. The observer struct itself is a zero-field unit struct (`pub struct XObserver;`) implementing only `Observer`. Shared predicates (`is_awaiting_approval`, `already_approved`, `active_spec`) live in ONE observer module and are imported by the others (`use super::approval_marker_observer::{...}`) rather than re-derived, so the several doors can never disagree about the state window. Every write goes through the shared `marker_body`/`write_atomic` helpers, never a hand-composed string. Tests are extensive and colocated at the bottom, split into pure-function unit tests (the recognizer/notice builders) followed by end-to-end `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` cases over a `tempdir()` fixture, each pinning one field incident by name in a doc comment.

## How to apply

A new observer is a new file under `hooks/observe/` (or the matching hook-event subfolder) with a unit struct implementing `Observer`, registered wherever the crate wires observers for its trigger. Open the module with a `//!` doc enumerating the numbered facts that must ALL hold, explicitly naming what makes the triggering signal unforgeable and any forged-input case it must reject. Reuse existing predicates from sibling observer modules instead of re-deriving equivalent logic. `observe()` must never panic and never return anything but `()`; every filesystem write inside it is best-effort (`let _ = ...`). Add unit tests for the pure recognizer logic first, then integration tests over a `tempdir()` project asserting both the positive mint and the fail-closed non-mint cases named in the module doc.

## Examples

Ref: apps/rt/src/hooks/observe/plan_approval_observer.rs
```rust
impl Observer for PlanApprovalObserver {
    fn observe(&self, input: &HookInput, ctx: &Ctx) {
        let cwd = ctx.project_dir_or_cwd(input);

        // Fact 1 — an unapproved Full spec in PLAN, else nothing is pending.
        let Some(spec) = active_spec(&cwd, input) else {
            return;
        };
        if !is_awaiting_approval(&cwd, &spec) || already_approved(&cwd, &spec) {
            return;
        }

        // Fact 2 — a clear plan-mode approval.
        if !plan_approved(input) {
            return;
        }

        // Both facts hold → record the genuine approval, best-effort.
        if let Some(marker) = approval_marker_path(&cwd, &spec) {
            let body = marker_body(
                &spec,
                "ExitPlanMode",
                input.session_id.as_deref().unwrap_or("unknown"),
                &mustard_core::time::now_iso8601(),
            );
            let _ = mustard_core::io::fs::write_atomic(&marker, body.as_bytes());
        }
    }
}
```

Ref: apps/rt/src/hooks/observe/approval_marker_observer.rs
```rust
/// `true` when `spec` is still in stage `Plan` (from its `meta.json`) — the one
/// lifecycle state where a PLAN approval is pending, and therefore the one where
/// a genuine approval gesture has anything to record.
pub(crate) fn is_awaiting_approval(cwd: &str, spec: &str) -> bool {
    let Some(sp) = ClaudePaths::for_project(Path::new(cwd))
        .and_then(|p| p.for_spec(spec))
        .ok()
    else {
        return false;
    };
```

        let Some(prompt) = user_typed_text(input) else {
            return;
